title: Buffet-line broadcast: one DRAM read feeds every accelerator
idea: One buffet tray serves every diner. Likewise, a weight-streaming memory node reads each weight block once and puts it on a shared multidrop optical/SerDes broadcast bus. All N data-parallel accelerators in the pod latch it at the same moment, in a synchronized schedule.
why: Data-parallel inference replicas all read the same weights. Broadcasting cuts DRAM reads and weight capacity N-fold: 8 replicas share one copy, freeing ~7/8 of weight HBM for KV cache.

title: Poor man's HBM on commercial HDI substrates
idea: Substitute the silicon interposer with a commercial mSAP HDI board (15 um lines) carrying bare LPDDR5X dies flip-chipped within 3 mm of an FPGA/ASIC, running a 1024-bit bus at a modest 2-3 Gb/s per pin.
why: Cost per bit and capital: roughly HBM2-class bandwidth at LPDDR cost without TSVs or scarce CoWoS capacity.

title: 3D-NAND toolset builds channel-hole gain cells with no EUV
idea: Ideal: density from tier count with tools already paid for. Closest: in a NAND-style oxide/word-plate stack, each channel hole holds two concentric ALD oxide-semiconductor devices per tier: an outer write channel charging an isolated metal ring, and an inner read channel gated by that ring, so every tier crossing is a capacitorless 2T gain cell built with the 3D NAND etch, ALD and staircase flow.
why: Facts 2 and 4: 100+ tiers at DUV pitch in existing NAND fabs with no capacitor and no EUV; bit cost could follow NAND-like layer economics if speed and retention hold.
note: Concentric write/read oxide devices per channel hole gives NAND-like layer economics; doubt: IGZO speed, ring isolation, retention at tier pitch.

title: Token-sweep restore: inference reads replace refresh, shortening capacitors
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: in LLM-inference memory every weight row is activated once per decode step (~10-16 ms) and each activation restores the cell, so the controller disables refresh and guarantees the sweep period; if serving pauses beyond the bound it drops the weights and reloads them from flash, keeping refresh power exactly zero.
why: Zero refresh power and bandwidth (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth today); a guaranteed ~16 ms window vs 64 ms cuts required Cs ~3x, so capacitor AR falls from ~70:1 to ~25:1, deleting support-mesh masks and halving HAR etch time (facts 1, 3, 4).

title: Apical-meristem nanowires grow stacked transistors along their own axis
idea: Shoots add segments at the tip; grow vertical Si nanowires by catalyst-tip (VLS) growth from the pad lattice while switching dopant and Ge gases every ~25 nm, so each wire holds 16 axial n+/p/n+ transistor segments, then fill around the forest with alternating spin-on dielectric and conductor layers that become wordline tiers timed to the segments.
why: Channels for all 16 tiers come from one growth run instead of patterning; at ~40 nm wire pitch that is ~100 nm2 per bit, ~8-10x bits/mm2 at roughly flat cost (fact 2).
note: All tiers' channels from one VLS growth; aligning wordline tiers to dopant segments and catalyst contamination are the doubt.

title: Myelin multilamellar self-assembly lays down twenty tiers in one coat
idea: Schwann cells wrap axons in dozens of uniform lamellae; spin a high-chi lamellar block copolymer that orders parallel to the substrate into 20+ layers (~12 nm period), then use sequential infiltration synthesis to turn one block into AlOx insulator and the other into In2O3 channel, creating a whole tier stack in one coat-anneal-infiltrate sequence below 200 C.
why: Tier-stack cost drops from ~100 depositions to one coat plus a few infiltration cycles; 40+ BEOL-compatible tiers with a single hole/slit patterning give ~10x bits/mm2 at near-flat cost (facts 2, 4).
note: 40 tiers from one coat; SIS oxides are device-poor, and 12 nm period leaves no room for wordlines.

title: Smoke detector: radioisotope micro-battery keeps low-leakage cells alive for decades
idea: Random stimulus 'smoke detector' (a tiny Am-241 source runs for decades) -> a Ni-63 or tritium betavoltaic cell in the module package supplies microwatts forever, refreshing an ultra-low-leakage gain-cell array whose retention is ~1000 s. Data survives loss of external power for ~decades with no new memory material.
why: Non-volatility comes from the package, with zero new process modules or fab capex. At 1000 s retention, refresh for a 16 Gb die is ~0.7 uW, which is within betavoltaic output, and the array keeps DRAM-class speed and unlimited endurance.
note: Package isotope keeps a 1000 s gain-cell array alive; doubts are periphery standby leakage and isotope regulation.

title: Coaxial gallium-oxide 2T0C cell grown inside one vertical hole
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: in a 3D-NAND-like stack of word planes, one DUV-printed hole receives nested ALD shells at each tier recess - an outer amorphous Ga2O3 write channel gated by the plane, a metal storage-node ring, a thin dielectric, and an inner Ga2O3 read channel gated by that ring.
why: Ga2O3's 4.8 eV gap gives off-current below ~1e-21 A, so retention exceeds years and refresh is zero with no capacitor module; one hole mask serves 32-64 tiers, raising density without EUV (facts 2, 3, 4).
note: Refresh-free multi-tier gain cell from one hole; ALD amorphous Ga2O3 mobility and nested-shell control are the doubt.

title: Tree-ring shells: coaxial gain cell in every tier-hole crossing
idea: Etch one array of vertical holes through a 100-layer wordline/oxide stack, then grow concentric shells like annual rings: an outer IGZO write-channel ring, a metal storage ring cut into per-tier segments by a selective recess, and an inner read-channel 'heartwood' that the storage ring gates. Each hole-tier crossing becomes a capacitorless 2T0C cell.
why: One hole litho and etch serves all tiers, as in 3D NAND; at ~100 nm hole pitch and 100 tiers that is ~100 nm2 per bit, ~8-10x planar DRAM bits/mm2 at roughly flat wafer cost, with no capacitor (facts 1, 2).
note: One hole litho for all tiers, ~8-10x bits/mm2; doubt: per-tier storage ring segmentation and reading floating-gated series channel.

title: Pollen-tube confined epitaxy grows monocrystalline channels in every tier
idea: A pollen tube grows only inside the style's channel; deposit a cheap 120-pair PECVD oxide/nitride stack as in 3D NAND, strip the nitride through slits to leave tunnels, then grow single-crystal Si into all tunnels at once by template-confined lateral epitaxy seeded from the substrate at each slit base.
why: Replaces slow, strain-limited Si/SiGe epitaxial superlattices (capped near 30-60 layers) with 3D-NAND-cost stacks, making 120 tiers (~10x bits/mm2) affordable at near-flat wafer cost (fact 2).
note: Single-crystal Si grown into NAND-style nitride-strip tunnels; lateral confined-epi distance and defects are the doubt.

title: Vertical codewords across tiers break 3D DRAM yield compounding
idea: Combine 3D NAND-style tier stacking with tier-orthogonal coding: each codeword takes one symbol from each of ~32 tiers along the vertical bitline, so a defective tier (lateral-transistor shorts, capacitor voids) costs only one symbol per codeword. Per-tier yield can then be 99% rather than 99.99%.
why: Tier-yield compounding is a hidden blocker for 26+ tiers (fact 2). Relaxed per-tier yield permits faster deposition, fewer inspections and ~2x more tiers per stack.

title: Josephson-era missing memory: 77 K thin-oxide 3D NAND as DRAM
idea: IBM's Josephson program (cancelled 1983) and later cryogenic computing stalled for lack of dense, cheap cold memory. At 77 K leakage collapses, so a 3D NAND-style vertical string with a 1.5-2 nm direct-tunneling oxide instead of ~7 nm Fowler-Nordheim oxide programs at ~3-5 V in tens of ns, suffers little hot-carrier wear and holds charge for hours.
why: Meets 100x: NAND cost structure (~$0.03-0.08/GB) with near-DRAM write speed, refresh-free hours retention and ~1e12-class endurance. Trade: liquid-nitrogen cooling (~10-15% facility overhead).
note: NAND cost with near-DRAM writes; doubt: direct tunneling through 2 nm oxide is temperature-insensitive, so hours retention is unlikely.
